review: S01 synthetic Metal4 GPU boundary protocol harness, static read-only review
execution: Reviewer did not compile or run the helper. Parent reports compiled-only; GPU run remains pending.

coverage.detail: An actual PlainVS/BoundaryFS one-pixel Fragment draw writes input0 before the checkpoint. A separate Blit writes input1. Only the eight G Vertex draws sample the five inputs; the four A draws use PlainVS and have no reads of them.

The checkpoint repeats the production Fragment|Dispatch|Blit to Blit and Blit to Vertex|Fragment|Dispatch stage masks. The split route ends A after Fragment-to-queue-Fragment, reopens the same Load/Store color/depth/stencil attachments, then waits queue-Fragment-to-Fragment; the one-pass route omits this split.

Each of 128 deterministic seeds compares complete BGRA8, Depth32Float, and Stencil8 byte arrays for one-pass versus split. Nonzero attachment changes, a Grass-only stencil value, and a final center-pixel stencil 12 witness reject no-draw outcomes.

The last G draw is opaque white at depth 0.01 and covers the center. Its BGRA channels must equal the CPU-calculated average of the five Vertex reads within one byte; that average includes both the Fragment-produced texel and Blit-produced texel. Snapshot readback must equal pre-scene initial depth, proving its Blit occurred before A/G scene writes.

Textures, buffers, argument tables, allocator, residency set, command, event and queue remain retained through event and feedback waits before readback. Each command submission registers all image and constant-buffer allocations.

limits: This is a synthetic one-sample 64x64 protocol test, not byte parity for the actual GameDecal/GroundDecal/particle/sky/Grass shaders or a proof of S01 runtime gate eligibility.

The snapshot image is read back to verify timing but is not a Grass Vertex input; the GPU test exercises the checkpoint ordering masks and the separate Fragment and Blit source inputs, not a Grass read from the snapshot itself.
Byte equality does not measure whether Grass Vertex work actually overlaps A Fragment work or whether the optimization improves frame time.

The helper does not test production source-owner callbacks, resource alias rejection, cancellation, failure quarantine, surface changes, or multisampling; those remain covered by source review and owner-run engine validation.
remaining: Owner may run the bounded GPU protocol helper under the fresh isolation gate, then validate the actual signed engine candidate separately.
